is the self-proclaimed and the sworn enemy of Dragon God Orsted. Initially a supporting character, aiding Rudeus with helpful advice, he later becomes the overarching antagonist of the series following the revelation that he actually sought to prevent the birth of Rudeus' children, who are prophesied to defeat him in the future. == Appearance==
He has a blank white face coupled with a grin that eludes memory, which gives off the feeling that his face is covered in a mosaic. ==Personality==
Hitogami appears friendly and casual when communicating with his apostles, but he is actually a manipulative trickster who pulls strings behind the scenes. He seems to derive a sick sense of enjoyment from tricking people into destroying what they value the most, and laughing at their despaired faces afterwards. He is also a sore loser that throws tantrums when things aren't going his way. ==Background==
Hitogami's exact origins is unknown. It is known that after the Creator God's death, unbeknownst to anyone, he was born within the Void World. At some point in the distant past, the being who would come to be known as Hitogami killed or otherwise usurped the original Human God and took his form.

Fate, also known as Destiny, is the rough history of the path an individual takes in their life. ==Background==

Like Mana, Fate is possessed by all beings in the universe of Mushoku Tensei even during the Six-Faced World Era but very few beings are able to see fate and try to influence it. Due to Orsted being in a timeloop made by the First Dragon God, Orsted has seen the past and knows the future of nearly everyone in the Human World, as such he refers to the original timeline history to be pre-ordained by Fate and he acts to ensure that original timeline is followed as much as possible against his upcoming battle against Hitogami. ==Strong Fate==
The path of history of individuals who are protected by a strong fate's cannot be altered easily and despite multiple attempts to alter it, not even by Gods. But the strength of fate can also be ambiguous especially during pregnancy of the individual. Another exception is when a massive calamity occurs like the Teleport Incident which could also cause the death even those protected by a strong fate. ===Notable Individuals with Strong Fate===
====Rudeus Greyrat====

Rudeus is protected by an unusually strong fate that when Hitogami tries to influence the course of events involving him, it rarely works out.

Gods are the most powerful beings on the Six-Faced World, and the original guardians of each world. Unlike the other beings that followed with the title of "God" such as the Seven Great Powers, these are actual beings of divine origins and are worshipped by the denizens of their respective worlds as deities. ==History==
=== Creation ===
After the Creator God created the Six-Faced World, he decided to use what was left of his power to split his body into 6 pieces and form divine beings who will ensure that all six worlds would prosper and to keep the worlds in balance. These six beings would come to be known as Gods to the people of their respective world. === Age Of The Gods ===
At the suggestion of the Human God, all the Gods formed a council to share information and knowledge with each other to benefit their worlds. The Gods would regularly meet, trade information, and discuss the state of the Six-Face World. === The God Wars ===
The God Wars (not the official name) began when the first Dragon God declared war on 4 of the 6 worlds in order to search for the murderers of his wife, Lunaria.

was a powerful demon who waged war against humanity 500 years ago before being sealed by the Seven Great Heroes. He was originally one of the Five Dragon Generals, the most powerful members of the Dragon Tribe who served as the First Dragon God's confidants. After escaping the destruction of the Dragon World, Laplace became the Second Dragon God. But during the Second Human-Demon War he was split into Demon God Laplace and Technique God Laplace by the Fighting God. While it is mentioned that he will be revived some time in the future, neither of his two halves actually appear in the main story. == Appearance ==
 
Being born with Dragon Tribe and Demon blood, Demon Dragon King Laplace before he was split in two was described as over 2 meter tall with silver hair with patches of green but has lesser scales compared to those of the Dragon Tribe. In addition he had fangs, claws. a set of wings, transparent white skin and two golden eyes. Demon/Magic God Laplace was described to have emerald green hair, and gentle eyes.

is the current Dragon God, a title given to the strongest member of the Dragon Tribe, and the sworn enemy of "Human God". ==Appearance==
Similar to other Dragon Race people such as Perugius, Orsted has silver hair and golden eyes with an overpowering look. He carries no visible equipment and wears a white coat adorned with fur. ==Personality==
Due to possessing a curse that causes nearly all living beings who see him to instinctively fear, hate, or distrust him, Orsted has poor social skills and generally maintains a distant, reserved attitude. Because ordinary interaction is extremely difficult for him, he has had few opportunities to develop normal relationships, leaving him blunt, quiet, and somewhat awkward when attempting to communicate outside of practical matters. His intimidating presence and naturally serious demeanor only reinforce this impression, even when he has no hostile intentions. When dealing with his primary objective, however, Orsted is absolutely ruthless. His goal of defeating Hitogami takes priority over almost everything else, and he is willing to destroy anything that directly stands in the way of accomplishing it, regardless of who or what it may be. This is especially apparent in his treatment of Hitogami's apostles.

is the former leader of the Superd's Warrior group who once served under Laplace with unwavering loyalty. He was accompanying Rudeus and Eris but left in search of his people. Under manipulation, Ruijerd killed his son, who was able to free him from Laplace's control. Following the annihilation of his species, Ruijerd travels the world to dissolve the stigma against the Superd race. ==Appearance==
Ruijerd is tall for an average Superd, muscular build, handsome and shared their distinctive features such as porcelain white skin and emerald green hair with a red gemstone on his forehead. He wears a brown tribal vest that only covers his back and sides, fully displaying his frontal torso and arms. Moreover, he is distinguished by his smooth oval chin and a long scar that trails from the right top corner of his forehead across his glabella to the left end of his cheek. When Rudeus bleached his hair, it became a different color. However, Ruijerd later shaved his head bald and wore a headband to cover the gemstone on his forehead.

is the main protagonist of Mushoku Tensei. He was an overweight 34-year-old Japanese NEET who is reincarnated into another world after being hit by a truck whilst saving some kids. Realizing he wasted away his previous life, he resolves to live this new one to its fullest and the series revolves around how he impacts his new world all whilst slowly growing out of his reclusive ways. ==Appearance==
Rudeus stands at around average height (175cm), has a muscular body despite being a magician, and his looks weren't that poor when his family members are asked. He was born with light brown hair and green eyes. However, he later has Kishirika Kishirisu switch out both of his original eyes for demon eyes, causing them to be heterochromatic. Like his father, Paul, Rudeus also has a mole underneath his left eye and follows his ponytail hairstyle as he grows older. He is also always seen wearing gray robes but rarely covers his head during his time as an adventurer. At a young age, he is careless about the outfit he wears due to traveling the Demon Continent.

The Teleport Incident, also known as Metastasis Event, is a Mana calamity that occurred in the Fittoa Region, Asura Kingdom in K417 which resulted in its citizens being teleported to random locations on the world. The incident caused an innumerable amount of casualties and was the first turning point in Rudeus Greyrat's life in the series. ==Prelude==

thumb|right|300px|Red Orb appearing above the Boreas Estate
Since the era of the Six-Faced World, numerous teleportation incidents has already occurred but in a smaller scale which is also one of the reasons why there is animosity between the worlds because of suspicions of one world might be invading the other for the disappearance of their people or appearance of monsters. But according to the Dragon Tribe researchers' hypothesis: a power possessed by every living creature permeates the Six Worlds which is called Dragon Battle Aura by the Dragon Tribe while the Demons call it Mana or Magic Power that is said to maintain a natural equilibrium within the Six Worlds. However, the power of the Six Worlds suddenly declined, creating significant imbalances.

The Teleportation Labyrinth (転移の迷宮) is an S-ranked labyrinth located beneath the desert of the Begaritt Continent that is accessed by a cave of a cliff north of the city of Rapan. ==Background==
 
250px|right|thumb|A group of Tarantula Deathlords guarding the Teleportation Circles
Like all Labyrinths near Rapan, the Teleportation Labyrinth is formed by ants that ate the remains of a gigantic Behemoth, previously slain by North God Kalman II and his group. The mutant descendants of these ants dig tunnels beneath the Behemoth's remains that eventually became Labyrinths where monsters became attracted to it because of their concentration of Mana and due to the labyrinth having numerous Teleportation Circles, it became known as the Teleportation Labyrinth. As with all Labyrinths, the Teleportation Labyrinth has its Magic Crystal located at the Seventh Floor where its monsters tend to kill or take intruders captive into the Magic Crystal where they become the "heart" of the Labyrinth that distribute Mana to all its inhabitants and allowing it to function.

I Don't Want to Die (死にたくない Shinitakunai) is the sixth episode of the second season (31st overall) Mushoku Tensei anime series originally broadcasted on August 13, 2023. ==Synopsis==
Rudeus continues his studies at Ranoa Magic Academy as he deepens his relationship with Fitts who joins him on investigating the Teleport Incident. At the Academy, there is also Zanoba who considers Rudeus as a doll figurine master asks to learn how to create them so at the advise of Fitts, they go to the slave market looking for someone they can teach Earth Magic for Zanoba, who is struggling to make dolls because of his Miko strength. ==Plot==
Rudeus begins to get used to school life in the university, where he studies magic he lacks experience in as well as researches the cause of the teleportation disaster alongside Fitz. However, Rudeus begins to realize he may have a crush on Fitz, much to his confusion since he still believes Fitz is male. Meanwhile, he also attempts to teach Zanoba how to create his own sculptures, but his own lack of magic capacity and his super strength prevent him being able to sculpt. Fitz suggests that Zanoba purchase a slave who can create sculptures for him. Rudeus, Fitz, and Zanoba then travel to the local slave market. Through Febritto, they purchase a young dwarf girl they name Julie.

The are a ranking of seven warriors recognized among the strongest in the world. The system was established by the Technique God around the end of the Second Human-Demon War. Unlike a continuously updated measure of combat strength, the Seven Great Powers functions through succession. Its positions change when a ranked Power is defeated or replaced, while the monuments associated with the ranking automatically reflect the resulting change. ==History==
===Establishment===
Around the end of the Second Human-Demon War, after Laplace had been divided into the Technique God and the Demon God, the Technique God established the Seven Great Powers. The provisional upper ranking was:

#Technique God
#Demon God
#Fighting God
#Dragon God

The identities of the original lower three positions have not been fully specified. The Technique God placed himself at the top of the ranking and established the other upper positions around the same period. ===Laplace War===
During the Laplace War, Dragon God Urupen, then ranked fourth, fought the second-ranked Demon God Laplace. Urupen's victory caused their positions to change, placing the Dragon God in second and the Demon God in fourth.
